summary: Invalid quantitative Appendix B preconditioning derivation directly motivates the core method; a corrected non-strict toy result is independently proved. Separate Minor issues affect the illustrative JAX interface and optional Angle-SAM radius. Empirical gains are not refuted.

problems.title: Inconsistent trace normalization invalidates the quantitative preconditioning derivation
problems.claim: Section 4.2 invokes Appendix B.1 to argue inverse-GGN preconditioning increases the functional-to-logit contribution; Equations 13–17 and r2>r1.
assumptions: Symmetric invertible freely independent random matrices A and B
Independent isotropic unit vector v; w=A^{-1}v
Finite second and inverse-second moments for corrected statement
problems.check: Exact identity certificate N=2,A=B=I; nonconstant spectrum A=Q diag(1,2) Q^T with independent uniform Q, B=I; normalized trace derivation and Cauchy–Schwarz.
problems.result: Identity: actual r1=r2=1, Eq13 gives 2=4, Eq16 gives 1=1/2, Eq17 gives intermediate2/final4 instead of1. Anisotropic actual r1=0.4,r2=0.625; printed expressions1.25/2.5. Correct r2=Etr(B^2)Etr(A^-2)/N^2 and r2/r1=Etr(A^2)Etr(A^-2)/N^2>=1.
problems.counterevidence: A corrected nondecrease result survives the toy assumptions. The first-order Functional-SAM decomposition remains valid. Actual Adam dynamics/normalized perturbations need not satisfy the model; authors acknowledge the approximation. No benchmark reversal demonstrated.
problems.impact: Major because a demonstrated invalid derivation directly supports a core proposed preconditioned method; whole-paper collapse and difficult repair are not required.

correction.statement: Use normalized trace consistently, unit norm E||AA^-1v||^2=1, and non-strict comparison with equality for constant squared spectral scale. Full practical transfer not proved.

problems.title: Illustrative JAX code uses an invalid keyword and reverses gradient/auxiliary outputs
problems.claim: Listing1 implements Functional-SAM using grad(loss_fn,hax_aux=True) and (dL_dlogits),dL_dtheta unpacking.
assumptions: JAX grad has_aux convention documented in official API actually viewed
Loss auxiliary is the unperturbed logit-loss cotangent
No missing helper or historical environment is assumed
problems.check: Official signature and return order; independent smooth scalar F(theta)=theta^2, loss(z)=z^2/2, theta=2.
problems.result: Correct return pair(parameter gradient,aux)=(16,4); swapped VJP at rho0.1 is67.2 instead of16.8, even though both normalized perturbation signs agree.
problems.counterevidence: With correct has_aux and (dL_dtheta,dL_dlogits) unpacking the VJP matches Eq11. Full wrappers were not supplied; this listing is not bound to historical training execution.
problems.impact: Minor, scoped to the implementation illustration; does not establish historical experiment failure.

correction.statement: dL_dtheta,dL_dlogits=grad(loss_fn,has_aux=True)(params), with correct auxiliary definition. No runnable JAX repair certified because JAX/helper/wrapper unavailable.

problems.title: Angle-SAM at pi/4 matches a rescaled SAM radius
problems.claim: Appendix D states phi=pi/4 recovers SAM to first order at the same radius.
assumptions: Smooth loss, nonzero gradient and normalized perturbation
problems.check: Binary cross-entropy logits(theta,0), first-class target, theta0: exact SAM and Angle-SAM derivatives.
problems.result: Angle correction is rho(HG+HF)u/sqrt2 instead of rho(HG+HF)u. At rho0.1 gradients -0.5176629528548886 and -0.52497918747894. Difference/rho tends(1-1/sqrt2)/4, not0.
problems.counterevidence: Angle-SAM is an optional future extension, not the main experimental method. Phi0 Functional-SAM is unaffected.

correction.statement: Angle-SAM radius rho corresponds to SAM radius rho/sqrt2; Angle-SAM radius sqrt2*rho matches SAM radius rho only to first order.

repair_verification: Corrected toy nondecrease theorem and Angle-SAM radius statement proved; JAX local interface repair checked statically, not executed.
limitations: No author code or training was executed; no empirical values independently reproduced.
